Evidence.description:
One checked claim, kept out of the prose and referenced from it.

The text of a finding stays readable: a claim carries one marker, `[3]`, or an
embedded link to `#ev-3`, and the pointer itself lives here. A pointer is to the
exact place, pinned to a commit: a file or a branch moves, and evidence that moved
no longer proves anything. The quote is required so the entry still says something
to a reader who cannot open the source.

command.description: kind=command or test: exactly what was run
command.title: Command

commit.description: kind=read: the commit the lines are read at
commit.title: Commit

path.description: kind=read: the file, relative to the repository root
path.title: Path

quote.description: Verbatim: the lines read, or the output of the command or test
quote.title: Quote

repo.description: kind=read: which repository `path` is in, when the system spans more than one. A short stable name, e.g. 'payments-api' or 'org/payments-api'; empty for a single-repository system. `keel recheck --repo NAME=PATH` maps it to a checkout
repo.title: Repo

url.description: Optional permalink to the same lines. Must be https, on a host in the organisation's evidence_hosts, and contain the commit: anything else is refused on save
url.title: Url

Evidence.title: Evidence

OrgFact.description: One statement, who stood behind it, and what it rests on.

confirmed_by.description: The person who confirmed it: 'Name <email>' or a role
confirmed_by.title: Confirmed By

confirmed_on.description: YYYY-MM-DD, the day it was confirmed
confirmed_on.title: Confirmed On

documents.description: Links to the documents it rests on (an architecture page, a policy), or their names when there is no link
documents.title: Documents

evidence.description: Code it rests on, in the same shape as report evidence, so `keel recheck org/<file>.yaml --repo PATH` says whether the lines are still there
evidence.title: Evidence

id.description: Cited as org:<file>#<id>; stable once cited
id.title: Id

statement.description: The fact, in one or two sentences
statement.title: Statement

systems.description: Optional: ids of the assessed systems that rely on it
systems.title: Systems

OrgFact.title: OrgFact

description: One platform or one policy, and the facts about it.

about.description: What this platform or policy is, so an assessor can tell whether it applies
about.title: About
